fixtureSha256.description: SHA-256 of the case fixture tree as it stood when this run executed. Optional: bundles predating the field are unbound rather than backfilled, since a backfilled hash would assert something nobody measured.

graderSha256.description: SHA-256 of the grader file that scored this run. Optional: bundles predating the field are unbound rather than backfilled. Graders import Node built-ins only, so the file fully determines the scoring.

checkerSha256.description: SHA-256 of the checker the case declares, when it declares one; null otherwise. Three graders execute a checker while scoring, so a checker edit moves their verdicts with the grader file unchanged. Checkers require Node built-ins only, so the file is the whole dependency.

stagedInputSha256.description: SHA-256 of the .agent-input tree staged for this condition (skill text or checker); null for control and policy, which stage nothing.

transcriptReducedAt.description: When transcript.jsonl was reduced to the shapes scripts/lib/reduce-transcript.mjs emits — tool-call commands, agent messages, and the model's final answer text. A harness transcript is a recording of a session on someone's machine, and the incidental half of it (working directory, installed skills, account tier, whatever a command printed) accumulates across hundreds of committed bundles: an audit on 2026-09-08 found a username in 1,890 places and a private host's tooling listed in 49 files. Reduction publishes the model's turn and drops the machine. A timestamp rather than a flag, because the two ways a bundle gets here are worth telling apart: reduced at capture reads close to finishedAt, while a bundle converted in the retroactive pass reads much later than the run it describes. eval-verify checks the claim rather than trusting it, so a full transcript cannot be committed under this field. Absent on bundles predating reduction, which are unreduced and say so by omission.

regrade.description: Present when this bundle's grading.json was recomputed by scripts/eval-rehome.mjs rather than written by the run that produced the outputs. The harness output is untouched and every input digest still binds; what moved is the grader that read it. Absent on every bundle whose verdict came from its own run, so the two can never be confused. Only control and policy may carry it: their treatment does not depend on the suite, so a grader repair is the only thing that changed. A skill or checker arm scored by a grader it never met would also have been STAGED differently, and no amount of re-scoring recovers that.
